description.narrative: The events in Gaza, with Israel's war against Hamas, have led to the dramatic destruction of buildings in Gaza. According to an assessment by United Nations Development Program (UNDP, April 2024), some 137,297 buildings were damaged, comprising more than half of the total. Of these, just over a quarter were destroyed, the remainder moderately to severely damaged.Massive landfill sites would be necessary to dump the rubble, depending on how much could be recycled. UNDP puts the cost for moving the rubble at US$500-US$600 million.Rebuilding these destroyed homes could take until 2040 in the most optimistic scenario, with total reconstruction across the territory costing as much as US$40-US$50 billion (UNDP 2024).To retrieve acceptable and affordable housing for Gaza's inhabitants, large scale reconstruction will be required. To the extent possible, the re-use of any available materials of damaged and destroyed buildings should be exploited.Currently, the knowledge of circular (re-)construction options and related available technology is limited in Gaza. This project will focus on the possibilities of circular re-use of demolished building materials and will include best practices for low carbon design of buildings in order to obtain future proof buildings for the years to come.Capacity building visits to the Netherlands of local Gazan and neighbouring governments and construction sector for the purpose of capacity building and knowledge exchange in the mentioned themes should benefit the companies and citizens of Gaza in their effort to rebuild their homes and society.
